This marked the largest percentage increase for a season not impacted by COVID-19 since the league expanded to 30 teams in 1998. The average attendance per game also saw a notable increase of 9.1% to 29,295, representing the largest single-season growth in 30 years. Overall, it was the first time the league's total attendance surpassed the 70 million mark since 2017. <3> On September 29, 2023, the Detroit Tigers formally announced that Miguel Cabrera, following his retirement at the conclusion of the 2023 season, would take on a new role as a special assistant to the president of baseball operations, Scott Harris. He joins an elite group that includes Jose Canseco (1988), Barry Bonds (1996), Alex Rodriguez (1998), and Alfonso Soriano (2006). Already having a historic season, Acuña Jr. had previously become the first player in MLB history with 30 home runs and 60 stolen bases. He did not stop at 40-60, however. On September 27, 2023, he stole his 70th base, creating the unprecedented 40-70 club. In a vintage performance at Busch Stadium, the 42-year-old pitched seven scoreless innings, allowing only four hits in the Cardinals' 1-0 win. The victory made Wainwright the 122nd pitcher in MLB history to reach the 200-win milestone. This achievement was a celebrated moment in a difficult season for both Wainwright and the Cardinals, drawing over 33,000 fans to witness the event. News of the milestone was widely reported the following day, September 19, 2023. <6> The Los Angeles Angels officially ended Shohei Ohtani's historic 2023 season on September 16, 2023, by placing the two-way superstar on the injured list with right oblique inflammation. This decision came after Ohtani had missed 11 consecutive games due to the injury, which he initially sustained during batting practice on September 4. The move concluded a remarkable season in which Ohtani was already not pitching due to a tear in his right ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) diagnosed on August 23. Despite the elbow injury, he had continued to serve as the designated hitter until the oblique issue arose. Ohtani finished the season with a .304 batting average, 44 home runs, and 95 RBIs, and as a pitcher, he held a 10-5 record with a 3.14 ERA. Their powerful offense set a new record for the highest team slugging percentage in a season at .501 and tied the 2019 Minnesota Twins for the most home runs in a single season with 307. [1, 2, 3] This was the first time two starting pitchers with at least 3,000 career strikeouts faced each other since 2007. [1] The two future Hall of Famers, who have a combined six Cy Young Awards, were teammates with the Detroit Tigers (2010-2014) and briefly with the New York Mets in 2023 before being traded to their respective Texas teams. [1, 4, 6] The game, which took place at Globe Life Field in Arlington, was a significant event in the American League West playoff race. [2, 3] Verlander and the Astros emerged victorious in the contest, with Scherzer taking the loss after allowing a season-high seven runs in three innings. [1] <9> ESPN announced its 29-game Major League Baseball schedule for September 2023, which was slated to be broadcast on ESPN+. The schedule commenced on September 1, 2023, with a game featuring the St. Louis Cardinals hosting the Pittsburgh Pirates. [1]

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The decision to award Atlanta the 2025 game was announced on November 16, 2023, after the city was previously set to host the 2021 All-Star Game, which was relocated by MLB. [4, 11, 13] <2> Major League Baseball announced on November 16, 2023, that the Atlanta Braves would host the 2025 All-Star Game and its associated festivities at Truist Park. [5, 10, 15] This decision comes after the 2021 All-Star Game was moved from Atlanta to Denver due to objections over changes in Georgia's voting laws. [2, 15] The 2025 Home Run Derby, a central event of All-Star Week, is scheduled to occur on Monday, July 14, 2025, at Truist Park in Atlanta. [3, 4, 6, 7] The 95th MLB All-Star Game itself will be held the following day, on Tuesday, July 15, 2025. [2, 9] <3> New York Yankees pitcher Gerrit Cole and San Diego Padres pitcher Blake Snell were named the winners of the 2023 American League and National League Cy Young Awards, respectively, on November 15, 2023. For Cole, it was his first Cy Young Award, and he won it unanimously, receiving all 30 first-place votes from the Baseball Writers' Association of America. Snell's victory marked his second Cy Young Award, making him the seventh pitcher in history to win the prestigious award in both leagues. He received 28 of the 30 first-place votes for the NL award. <4> Brandon Hyde of the Baltimore Orioles and Skip Schumaker of the Miami Marlins were named the 2023 American League and National League Managers of the Year, respectively, by the Baseball Writers' Association of America. [1, 12] Hyde earned his first Manager of the Year award after leading the Orioles to a remarkable 101-61 record, securing their first AL East title since 2014 and the team's first 100-win season since 1980. [4, 6, 9] He received 27 out of 30 first-place votes. [9] In his debut season as a manager, Schumaker guided the Marlins to an 84-78 record and their first postseason appearance in a full season since 2003. [1, 6, 8] This achievement made him the eighth manager in history to win the award in his first year. [2, 8] <5> Gunnar Henderson of the Baltimore Orioles and Corbin Carroll of the Arizona Diamondbacks were unanimously named the American League and National League Jackie Robinson Rookies of the Year, respectively. The announcement was made on November 13, 2023, by the Baseball Writers' Association of America (BBWAA). Henderson became the first player in Orioles history to win the award by a unanimous vote. Carroll was the first player in Diamondbacks franchise history to be named Rookie of the Year. This marked the fifth time both Rookie of the Year winners were unanimous selections. <6> The winners of the 2023 Louisville Slugger Silver Slugger Awards were revealed during a special broadcast on MLB Network on November 9, 2023. [1, 3] Voted on by MLB managers and coaches, the awards recognize the best offensive players at each position in both the American and National Leagues. [1, 3] For the first time since the award's inception in 1980, a team Silver Slugger Award was also presented to honor the best offensive team in each league. [2] <7> Major League Baseball and four former minor league teams settled three antitrust lawsuits that had been filed in both state and federal courts. [2] The lawsuits were initiated by the Tri-City ValleyCats, Norwich Sea Unicorns, Staten Island Yankees, and Salem-Keizer Volcanoes in response to MLB's 2020 reorganization and downsizing of the minor leagues, which they argued was an unlawful boycott. [2] The settlement, announced in November 2023, effectively ended a significant legal challenge that was on a path to the Supreme Court. [1, 3] This prevented a potential re-evaluation of MLB's century-old, court-granted exemption from antitrust laws, a legal precedent that was being contested as part of the lawsuit. [1, 2, 3] <8> In a surprising move, the Chicago Cubs hired Craig Counsell as their 56th manager on November 6, 2023, luring him away from the division-rival Milwaukee Brewers. The deal was a record-breaking five-year contract worth over $40 million, which made Counsell the highest-paid manager in MLB history at the time of the signing. This hiring was unexpected as the Cubs simultaneously announced the firing of manager David Ross, who had led the team for four seasons. Counsell, a Wisconsin native and the winningest manager in Brewers history, had led Milwaukee to five postseason appearances in the previous six years. His contract with the Brewers had expired on October 31, 2023, and while he was pursued by other teams like the New York Mets and Cleveland Guardians, his move to the rival Cubs was a stunner in the baseball world. <9> The winners of the 2023 Rawlings Gold Glove Awards, which honor the premier defensive players at each position in both the American and National Leagues, were announced on November 5, 2023. [1] The reveal took place during a special edition of ESPN's "Baseball Tonight." [2, 8] The 2023 class of winners included 13 first-time recipients. [2] The selection process for the awards is a combination of voting by MLB managers and coaches, which accounts for 75% of the total, and the SABR Defensive Index, which constitutes the remaining 25%. [3, 7]

After his stellar 2019 season, he signed a $245 million, seven-year contract but pitched only 31 1/3 innings afterward due to the injuries.
